body: Reference seam progress (bd-01M14K853WRGGZ2Y5YZ9KWXM6H): module instances now exist and are law-checked on JVM (JS/Native running). story.StoryRef = Situation | Segment | Entity | Context | Participant(situation, role, entity) | Temporal(from, relation, to, context) | Causal | Goal | StateChange | Reference | Containment(member, parent, kind) | EntityLink — i.e. every node and every stored edge is addressable; relation names are the enum case names, Custom roles/relations encode structurally ('custom', ns, label). features.FeatureAddress = Space | Observation(space, FeatureTarget) | Derivation(Checksum), with FeatureTargetKey.parts/parse public for reuse. document.DocRef = ChartNode | {Entity,Situation,Segment,Context}Mention | {…}Canonical (kind is a case, not a type parameter, so a closed sum serializes and kinds cannot cross). laws.AddressableLaws.addressable[A](name) is a Discipline rule set (round trip, tag, foreign-None, injective, wire round trip, no whitespace) wired into LawsSuite for CoreRef/StoryRef/FeatureAddress; DocRef is checked in document's own suite because laws does not depend on document (I did not touch build.sbt — that is yours for the view module; if you add laws dependsOn document while you are in there, I will move the DocRef check over). Files: story/…/ref.scala, features/…/address.scala, document/…/ref.scala, laws/…/AddressableLaws.scala, laws/…/AddressGens.scala (generators you can reuse for view tests), LawsSuite. For view: ViewRef = Core | Story | Feature | Doc (+ Recall/Align later) with parse dispatching on tag; nothing else is needed from me for CodexFlow's target field. Next on my side: recall/align instances and the covering/supporting read API on NarrativeGraph.
